# Asuka 0.3.0

First release since **0.2.0** (November 2022). This is a large, partly breaking
update: the detector API, the packaging and the internal scanner were all
modernised, the detector count grew from **9 to 18**, and Asuka learned to
resolve `import` statements across files.

Full history: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/wangbar0133/Asuka/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

---

## Highlights

- **18 detectors** (was 9) — the new ones cover unprotected `selfdestruct`,
  weak randomness, timestamp dependence, unchecked token transfers, arithmetic
  precision, tautological comparisons, bidi/RTL-override characters in source,
  deprecated Solidity constructs and dangerous unary expressions.
- **Cross-file scanning** — local imports are resolved into a project graph, so
  inheritance chains and declared types resolve across files. Detectors now see
  state variables inherited from a base contract even when it lives in another
  file.
- **Scan failures are isolated** — one unparsable file no longer aborts the
  whole run; failures are reported at the end with a red warning.
- **Strict parsing** — a file with syntax errors is reported as failed instead
  of silently producing an empty AST (which used to look like "no findings").
- **Modern development flow** — `pyproject.toml` packaging, 400 tests at 98%
  coverage, `ruff` linting, and CI on Python 3.11–3.14.

## ⚠️ Breaking changes

If you use Asuka as a library (rather than the `asuka` command), read this
section; the CLI itself is unchanged.

| What | Before | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Detector plugins | module-level `NAME`/`ID`/`DESCREIBE`/`ADVICE`/`RISK` + `check(scan)` | a `Detector` subclass (`vuls/detector.py`) with class attributes and `check(self, scan)`, registered in `vuls/all_detector.py` |
| Result field | `Vuls.descreibe` | `Vuls.description` |
| Constants | `DESCREIBE`, `METHED` | `DESCRIPTION`, `METHODS` |
| Packaging | `setup.py` + `requirements.txt` | `pyproject.toml` (both files removed) |
| Python | 3.9-era code | **3.11+** required |

Detectors are now stateless singletons in `ALL_DETECTORS`; use
`self.result(vul_list)` to build results and register new detectors in
`DETECTOR_CLASSES`. See `vuls/README.md` for the template and `AGENTS.md` for
the conventions.

| `SWC-115` | Authorization through tx.origin | High | |

| `202` | Imprecise Arithmetic Order | Medium | **new** |

## Cross-file scanning

Local imports are resolved automatically:

```solidity
import "./Base.sol";        // relative to the importing file
import "../shared/Lib.sol"; // relative to the importing file
import "/contracts/A.sol";  // relative to the scan root
```

Imported files are parsed and indexed so inheritance chains and declared types
resolve, and detectors can recognise a state variable inherited from a base
contract in another file — which fixes both a false positive (a variable typed
`address` reported as an unchecked token transfer) and a false negative (a
write to an inherited `mapping` after an external call was missed).

Imports are **resolution-only**: a dependency is never a scan target (directory
scans still cover every `.sol` inside the tree). Package-style paths such as
`"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol"` are recorded but not
resolved — there is no node_modules/remappings support yet. A *local* import
that cannot be found is reported as a warning:

```
2 import(s) not found:
  contracts/A.sol: ./missing/B.sol
```

Inherited **functions** are not scanned yet — only functions defined in the
files being scanned are reported.

## Reliability

- **Error isolation**: a file that fails to parse, or that crashes a detector,
  is collected in `Asuka.errors` and reported at the end of the run; the exit
  code stays 0 and the remaining files are still scanned.
- **Strict parsing**: the scanner uses `parse_file(..., strict=True)`, so
  syntax errors are surfaced instead of silently yielding an empty AST.
- **Casts are transparent**: calls nested inside elementary casts such as
  `uint8(sha3(...))` or `address(x)` were invisible to the scanner before —
  they are now extracted (this alone added findings on the bundled sample
  contracts).
- `view`/`pure` detection now uses `stateMutability` instead of `visibility`;
  the old check never matched and produced false positives on view functions.

## Fixed

- **Python 3.13+ support**: the vendored generated parser imported the removed
  `typing.io` module, so Asuka could not even be imported on 3.13/3.14.
- **Crashes**: bare `delegatecall(data)`; `require()` without arguments in the
  tx.origin detector; a `payable(x)` cast in the arbitrary-call detector;
  `Tools.scope_check` on single-line ranges; `get_below_statements` for nodes
  without a location.
- **Empty results**: `VulTable`/`print_summary` crashed when every scanned file
  failed; `Asuka.vul_count()` always returned 0.
- **Detector correctness**: compound pragmas (`^0.4.16 || ^0.5.0`) are now
  honoured by the integer-overflow detector; `merge_loc_list([])` no longer
  raises.
- **Security**: a hardcoded Etherscan API key was removed from the legacy test
  suite (it had been published since 2022 — rotate it if still active).

## Install

Requires Python 3.11+.

```shell
pip install "git+https://github.com/wangbar0133/Asuka.git@v0.3.0"
```

Or install an attached artifact:

```shell
pip install asuka-0.3.0-py3-none-any.whl
```

Asuka is not published on PyPI; the `asuka` console script is the entry point.

## Usage

```shell
asuka .                        # scan every .sol under the current directory
asuka contracts/Token.sol      # scan a single file
asuka . -i s107,101            # only these detectors
asuka . -e 204 -t 4            # exclude a detector, 4 worker processes
asuka -d                       # list the 18 detectors
asuka 0x… -c eth -k APIKEY     # fetch verified source from Etherscan
```

## Verification

- CI on the tagged commit: lint plus the test suite on Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13
  and 3.14 — all green.
- 400 tests, 98% line coverage over `core/`, `ast_scanner/`, `scraper/` and
  `vuls/`; detector behaviour is pinned by a 10-file × 18-detector matrix with
  exact expected counts.
- The attached wheel was installed into a clean Python 3.14 environment and
  smoke-tested: `asuka --version` → `0.3.0`, `asuka -d` → 18 detectors,
  `asuka test_data/` → 10 files / 36 findings, and a single-file target
  resolved its relative import without warnings.
